chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: Roy Milton's band and tenor Buddy Floyd
summary: Camille Howard, Roy's entertaining blues band, and Buddy Floyd's economy of notes that influenced his own slow blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: But anyway, I worked there with Roy Milton. It was nice. Camille Howard, she'd sing and play, and Roy would sing... They were a real entertaining Blues type of band. And the tenor player, Buddy Floyd, he really impressed me, the way he could get to an audience. Now, this guy could only play three or four notes in a solo. But what he could with those three or four notes was spectacular. In fact, I did some things not too long ago when I did a slow Blues thing, and I had him in my mind when I was playing this slow Blues thing on the record, the Slow Blues, you know -- because he could really lay back on one of those notes and moan on it. But as far as really moving around on the saxophone, nothin'!
Well, it's a thing that's not out yet, one of those slow blues things that I do with my big orchestra. I called them "Dirty Old Blues."

Okay, good! And this guy was really amazing, how he could move an audience! Like, I'm kind of fly. I'm running all up and down the saxophone and going on, you know.
